t: The structure of DNA: including nucleotides
o: I can describe the structure of DNA and how DNA is copied during mitosis.

t: Efficiency (in terms of energy and power)
o: I can calculate the efficiency of an energy transfer and describe ways in which energy is dissipated.

t: Concentration and rate: practical using gas collection method
o: I can carry out a fair test to investigate how the rate of reaction depends on the concentration of a reacting solution.

t: Common defects of the human eye
u: coordination and control the human nervous system
o: I can describe common defects of the eye and how we treat them.
I can identify that all cells have some structures in common and I can explain that all organisms are unicellular or multicellular.

t: The size and scale of cells: including standard form
o: You can describe numbers and sizes of cells using appropriate units and standard form.
I can describe what happens to the atoms of reactants as they form products in a chemical reaction.
I can plan and carry out a test to try to change the shape of different materials in different ways.

t: Adaptations of plants for photosynthesis: absorbing light
o: You can describe how plants are adapted to absorb light for photosynthesis.
I can describe how energy is transferred by a force and calculate the amount.
I can accurately measure the volume of an acid of an unknown concentration that neutralises an alkali of a known concentration.
I can describe the role of the human skeleton in support, protection and making blood cells.

t: Factors affecting the rate of photosynthesis
o: I can describe and explain the effects of various factors on the rate of photosynthesis.
I can represent and calculate the velocity of moving objects.

t: Animals are adapted for their environment
o: I can describe how some animals are adapted to help them survive, and how environmental conditions affect animal biodiversity.

t: Resistance of a wire at a constant temperature
o: I can describe how to investigate the resistance of a wire at a constant temperature and make scientific conclusions.

t: The importance of exchange surfaces and transport systems in humans
u: transport and exchange surfaces in humans
o: I can explain how exchange surfaces and transport systems enable cells in multicellular organisms to be quickly supplied with substances they need to stay alive.
I can plan an experiment to test the strength of an electromagnet and explain how different factors affect the strength of an electromagnet.
I can design a simple electrical circuit to detect water levels.

t: Conservation of mass and balanced symbol equations
o: I can explain the conservation of mass and write balanced chemical equations to show how the atoms of reactants in a chemical reaction are rearranged to form products.
I can describe the properties of alpha, beta and gamma radiation.

u: introduction to the human skeleton and muscles
o: I can carry out and review an investigation into muscle strength.

t: Classification into kingdoms and domains: sub-cellular evidence
o: I can describe the classification of organisms based on evidence from their phenotype and cells.
I can explain what happens when one metal displaces another metal from a salt, in solution as well as how carbon can be used to extract metals from ores.
I can explain chemical bonding in terms of the transfer or sharing of electrons.
I can safely and accurately measure the temperature of different objects using a thermometer.

t: The role of the skin in thermoregulation
u: coordination and control maintaining a constant internal environment
o: I can describe the roles of various parts of the skin in controlling human body temperature.

t: Analysing series circuits: including complex calculations
o: I can use circuit rules and the equation I = V ÷ R to analyse series circuits.
I can describe the key features of a plant adapted to suit its habitat.
I can investigate which materials are stretchy and explain how suitable they are for different uses.
I can describe and calculate the properties of a spring using Hooke’s law.

t: The energy of an object in a gravitational field (EP=mgh)
o: I can calculate the change in energy of an object because of its movement in a gravitational field.
I can predict the state of matter of a substance at different temperatures using the particle model.
I can describe in simple terms how fossils are formed.
I can identify independent, dependent, and control variables and describe the differences between them.
I can explain the pH scale and appropriately use universal indicator, phenolphthalein, methyl orange, and litmus and pH meters to identify different solutions.

u: coordination and control hormones and the human endocrine system
o: I can describe the causes and treatments for type 1 and type 2 diabetes.
I can plan and do an investigation to find out about waterproof materials.

t: Specialised cells are adapted for their functions
o: I can describe how specialised cells in animals and plants are adapted for specific functions.

t: Diffusion through a permeable material: practical
o: I can explain observations of diffusion through jelly cubes (a permeable material).
I can describe the properties of metals and relate these to a model of the structure of metals.

t: Moving into and out of the blood: diffusion, osmosis and active transport
u: transport and exchange surfaces in humans
o: I can explain how particles of substances move into and out of the blood by diffusion, osmosis and active transport.

t: Factors affecting the rate of photosynthesis
o: I can describe and explain the effects of various factors on the rate of photosynthesis.
I can identify and name natural and human-made light sources.
I can explain how to investigate the effect of force or mass on the acceleration of an object.
I am able to name the main gases in the atmosphere and describe the test and some uses for each one.
I can explain the shape of a heating/cooling curve by describing the energy changes through the heating/cooling of a substance.
I can complete a practical to measure the temperature change in a displacement reaction, record results, analyse data, and write a conclusion.
I can describe the structure and properties of a polymer.
I can describe the properties of alpha, beta and gamma radiation.

t: Virtual images from convex and concave lenses (including magnification)
o: I can describe the formation of virtual images by convex and concave lenses and draw ray diagrams to find the position and magnification of the image.
I can use chemical equations to identify and describe oxidation, decomposition and precipitation reactions.

t: Activity and half-life calculations (including complex ones)
o: I can interpret radioactive half-life graphs and make calculations using values of half-life.
I can label the parts of a rope or water wave that can be measured, and I can interpret and sketch scale drawings of transverse waves.
I can explain why electrolysis is required for the extraction of aluminium from its ore and describe the process.
I can explain what is meant by the spectrum of electromagnetic waves.
I can use dot and cross diagrams to explain how electrons are shared to form a covalent bond.
You can interpret and explain sound waves shown on an oscilloscope.

t: Modern periodic table and electron configuration
u: atomic structure and the periodic table
o: I can describe the way the modern periodic table is organised and draw the electronic configuration of the first twenty elements.

t: pH scale and universal indicator solution
o: I can measure the pH of an acid or alkali using the pH scale.
I can explain the properties, uses and dangers of non–ionising electromagnetic radiation.
I can describe the processes in the carbon cycle.

t: Observing the structure and distribution of stomata: practical
u: transport and exchange surfaces in plants
o: I can use a light microscope to observe imprints of stomata and investigate their distribution on leaves.

t: Calculating the energy of a moving object (Ek=½mv²)
o: I can calculate the energy an object has because it is moving.
I can accurately measure the acceleration of a dynamics trolley.
I can clearly describe how to measure speed and explain how I can do this accurately.
I can carry out tests for biological molecules, including sugars, starch, proteins and lipids.

t: Hormonal control of the menstrual cycle
o: I can explain the roles of FSH, LH, oestrogen and progesterone in controlling the menstrual cycle in human females.
I can explain why reflections (images) are seen in mirrors and describe the properties of mirror images.
I can explain that light travels in straight lines.

u: what plants do and what they need
o: I can ask relevant questions about what plants need and plan a comparative test to answer them.
I can describe the difference between a pure substance and a mixture.
I can make observations and describe how an animal grows and changes in its life cycle.
I can use simple models to explain what happens during photosynthesis, including a model of the two main stages.

t: Distance from sounds: do and review
o: I can carry out and evaluate a fair test about the volume of sounds.
I can identify high and low pitched sounds.
I can perform a practical to measure the temperature change in a neutralisation reaction, record results, analyse data, and conclude if the reaction is exothermic or endothermic.

t: Calculating the energy of springs (Ee = 1/2 ke²)
o: I can calculate the energy a spring has because it is stretched.

u: coordination and control hormones and the human endocrine system
o: I can describe the roles of the hormones adrenaline and thyroxine in the human body, and explain what is meant by negative feedback.

t: The cell cycle and cell division: mitosis
o: I can describe the phases of the cell cycle including mitosis.
I can create scientific diagrams of common laboratory equipment, showing how they are used together.

u: living things and where they live
o: I can explain why different animals live in different habitats.

u: why we group and classify living things
o: I can group micro-organisms based on similarities and differences.

t: The role of microorganisms in decomposition
o: I can explain the role of microorganisms and detritus feeders in decomposition.
I can describe the properties of diamond and graphite and explain how they result from their giant covalent structures, as well as relate them to their uses.
I can describe and explain when refraction happens and when total internal reflection happens at boundaries between media.

t: Ionic diagrams for binary ionic substances
o: I can draw dot and cross diagrams for binary ionic compounds.
I can explain what potable water is and describe how it can be obtained from groundwater and sea water.
I can identify a reactant as being in excess or the limiting reactant and use that information to calculate a theoretical yield.

t: What plants need to grow and stay healthy
o: You can set up an investigation to find out what happens to plants when they do not get what they need.
I can plan an investigation to see how changing the angle of a mirror affects the angle of reflected light.

t: The inheritance of biological sex in humans
o: I can explain how the inheritance of chromosomes determines biological sex in humans.
I can describe how electromagnets are used in a range of practical applications.
I can use the idea of resultant force to explain whether a change of speed occurs or not.
I can explain how a material’s specific heat capacity describes how easily it is heated or how much energy it transfers as it cools.
I can interpret and sketch displacement-time graphs of transverse waves.
I can explain how a floor can support a range of objects with very different weights.
I can describe and choose suitable methods to sample populations of plants or animals.
I can describe the impact of exercise on the human body.

t: Reactions of the halogens: including displacement practical
o: I can write word and symbol equations to show how Group 7 elements react.

t: Measuring the resistance of a diode
o: I can interpret an I–V graph of a diode in order to describe its properties.

t: Chemical reactions of acids with metals and metal carbonates
o: I can write balanced equations for acid – metal reactions, as well as acid - metal carbonate reactions, and predict the names and states of products.
I can make calculations using the equation E = m × L
I can describe the processes in the water cycle.
I can identify the organs of the human male and female reproductive system and describe the roles of the parts.

t: Light intensity and the inverse square law
o: I can explain why light intensity decreases further from a light source.

u: atomic structure and the periodic table
o: I can relate the atomic number and mass number to the structure of atoms of each element.
I can identify that sounds are made when something vibrates.
I can identify bases, predict the names and states of products from a neutralisation reaction and compare the properties of metal and non-metal oxides.
I can explain why it is important for a plant that its seeds are dispersed over a wide area, and carry out an experiment to measure seed dispersal.
I can describe what a mole is and its link with the Avogadro constant.

t: Models of single-gene inheritance: family tree diagrams
o: I can construct and interpret family tree diagrams showing information about inheritance of a feature.

t: Preparing and observing a microscope slide
o: I can prepare a microscope slide with a specimen of tissue, observe it using a microscope, and record my observations in a scientific line drawing.
I can explore the size, colour and features of a shadow, and compare shadows to reflections of objects.

t: Developing a reactivity series for metals
o: I can compare the reactions of different metals with water and dilute acids in order to work out the reactivity series for metals.
I can explain why some substances can diffuse through the cell membrane and others cannot.
I can use a simple food chain to show how animals and plants depend on each other for food.
I can describe how objects with a positive or negative charge attract or repel other charged objects.
I can measure the speed of sound waves in air using an echo method.
I can describe the properties of graphene and fullerenes, relating them back to their structures.

t: Measuring waves in a ripple tank
o: I can accurately measure the wavelength, frequency and wave speed of water waves in a ripple tank.
I know that changes of state are reversible changes.
I can explain why the survival of consumers depends upon photosynthesis in producers.

u: particle explanations of density and pressure
o: I can define density, calculate its value, and describe how to measure volume.
I can describe the action of acid with bicarbonate of soda as an irreversible change, where a new material is formed.

t: Modern periodic table and electron configuration
u: atomic structure and the periodic table
o: I can describe the way the modern periodic table is organised and draw the electronic configuration of the first twenty elements.

t: Ionic equations: reactions of Group 1 and Group 7
o: I can write balanced ionic equations and half equations for the reactions of Group 1 and 7 elements.
I can explain how energy can be transferred from the nuclei of atoms to cause heating.
I can describe and apply the relationship between mass and gravitational force.

t: Changing the speed of a parachute
o: I can clearly describe how drag forces affect the motion of falling objects.
I can explain the effect of greenhouse gases on the temperature of Earth’s atmosphere.
I can use circuit diagrams to build parallel circuits and draw circuit diagrams of parallel circuits.

t: Measuring the size and distribution of populations of organisms
o: I can describe how to identify species, estimate the population size of a species and how to investigate the effect of a factor on the distribution of this species.
I can explain how igneous rocks form and describe features of different types.
I can interpret and sketch graphs of longitudinal waves.
I can explain how a switch is used to open and close a circuit.
You can use the idea of the Moon's movement to begin to explain why the Moon appears to change shape.
